labelChirho: trace, draw (Qal: mark a boundary line)
descriptionChirho: Qal active form meaning to trace, draw, or mark out a boundary line. Cross-lingual evidence: Spanish 'trazó' (traced/drew), Hindi 'खींची/मुड़ी' (drew/turned), Arabic 'رَسَمَ/امْتَدَّ' (drew/extended), Korean '그었다/그렸다' (drew a line/drew), Swahili 'ukachora/ukazunguka' (you drew/you went around). The active Qal perfect describes the agent who performs the action of marking or delineating a boundary, typically in land descriptions.

Pual passive participle meaning 'the marked-out (boundary)' or 'that which has been delineated.' Distinct from the Qal active: English 'the marked-out,' Spanish 'extendiéndose' (extending itself), Hindi 'गोल' (round/circular), Arabic 'الْمُتَّصِلَةُ' (the connected/adjoining one), Korean '그렸다' (was drawn), Swahili 'uliotandazwa' (that which was spread out). The passive stem and participial form indicate the result state of being marked out rather than the act of marking.
